question: how much of the delivered next-category macro-F1 is the encoder's LEARNED component vs. features already separable at initialization

decomposition_vs_place_level.reading: roughly nine parts input granularity to one part learned graph training, on the category axis only

noise_floor.command: python scripts/integrity_v2/build_study_repr.py --state alabama --cell V18UT_INERT --repr-seed 42 --epochs 5 --device cuda --encoder resln --forward-only --add-continuous-time
noise_floor.protocol: run twice back-to-back, identical invocation, embeddings compared row-by-row
noise_floor.hardware: nespedgpu: NVIDIA RTX 6000 Ada Generation, driver 580.173.02, CUDA 13.0, PyTorch 2.11.0+cu128
noise_floor.portability: MEASURED PROPERTY OF THIS MACHINE + THIS DRIVER/TORCH COMBINATION -- NOT PORTABLE to other hardware or software versions
noise_floor.implication: reproducing the delivered substrate can only ever mean rebuilding within this noise, never matching bytes; a hash-based tamper check would falsely flag a legitimate rebuild
noise_floor.does_it_move_a_reported_digit: no -- seeds 0/1/7/42 are near-uncorrelated random draws (cosine ~0 to each other) yet only span 0.14pp (AL) / 0.15pp (AZ) of macro-F1; a perturbation many orders of magnitude smaller than a fully independent draw cannot move a two-decimal digit

caveats: category axis only -- region is untouched and carries the dissertation's strongest claims (TX +1.21, CA +1.06, non-inferiority at all six); never generalize this result to the substrate as a whole
does not show the representation is worthless -- shows the LEARNED component adds little on this axis; the check-in-level input structure vs. place-level still does the +1.45/+2.38 pp of real work
repr-seed 42 coincides with the delivered substrate's own init seed and is not fully independent of it (see per-seed cosine checks); seeds 0/1/7 are the clean floor
